headlines.title: Caterpillar (CAT) Taps Derrick York As Denise Johnson Sets Early 2027 Retirement
headlines.summary: Caterpillar (NYSE: CAT) said group president of Resource Industries Denise Johnson plans to retire in early 2027. The company named Derrick York, currently leading Solar Turbines and other roles inside Caterpillar, as her successor for Resource Industries. Johnson is credited by Caterpillar with reshaping its mining business during a historic downturn and delivering substantial financial improvements.

headlines.title: Learn Why The Bull Case For Caterpillar (CAT) Could Change Following AI Power Demand
headlines.summary: Caterpillar is investing about US$1b in North Carolina to expand Cat Compact manufacturing and has confirmed a US$1.63 quarterly dividend payable on November 19, 2026. Surging demand for Caterpillar power generation equipment tied to AI data centers has contributed to a record US$72b backlog, with orders reaching through 2030. We will now see how Caterpillar's investment narrative might be reshaped by the AI driven spike in power generation demand.

headlines.title: Caterpillar Set to Report Q3 Earnings: Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?
headlines.summary: CAT is poised for another quarter of earnings and revenue growth, backed by a $72 billion backlog and strong demand, but rising tariffs could pressure margins.

headlines.title: Caterpillar (CAT) Q3 Earnings Preview: What You Should Know Beyond the Headline Estimates
headlines.summary: Evaluate the expected performance of Caterpillar (CAT) for the quarter ended September 2026, looking beyond the conventional Wall Street top-and-bottom-line estimates and examining some of its key metrics for better insight.

headlines.title: Can Caterpillar’s $72B Backlog Save Its Stock From a 10% Slump?
headlines.summary: Caterpillar just posted its first ever $20 billion quarter, yet the stock has since fallen sharply and the October 29 earnings call will reveal whether a record backlog signals a rebound or a reckoning.

description: Caterpillar Inc. provides construction and mining equipment, off-highway diesel and natural gas engines, industrial gas turbines, and diesel-electric locomotives in the United States and internationally. The Construction Industries segment offers asphalt pavers, cold planers, compactors, forestry machines, material handlers, motor graders, pipelayers, road reclaimers, telehandlers, track-type tractors, and track and wheel excavators; backhoe, compact track, skid steer, track-type, and wheel loaders; and related parts and work tools. Its Resource Industries segment provides electric rope and hydraulic shovels, draglines, rotary drills, hard rock vehicles, mining trucks, wheel loaders, off-highway and articulated trucks, wide-body trucks, wheel tractor scrapers and dozers, and landfill and soil compactors; machinery components, and wear and maintenance components; and technology products and services for fleet management, equipment management analytics, autonomous machine capabilities, safety services, and mining performance solutions. The Energy & Transportation segment offers reciprocating engine powered generator sets; reciprocating engines, drivetrain, and integrated systems and solutions; centrifugal gas compressors and related services; and diesel-electric locomotive components, and other rail-related products. Its Financial Products segment provides operating and finance leases, revolving charge accounts, installment sale contracts, repair/rebuild financing, working capital loans, and wholesale financing; and insurance and risk management products and services. The All Other segment offers parts distribution; logistics and distribution services; electronics and control systems; dealer portfolio management; brand management and marketing strategy; and digital investment services. It also provides mining software solutions. The company was formerly known as Caterpillar Tractor Co. Caterpillar Inc. was incorporated in 1925 and is headquartered in Irving, Texas.
